variable (G) in
def aux (p : M) : OpenPartialHomeomorph M (OrbitSpace M G) :=
  Classical.choose (isLocalHomeomorph (G := G) (M := M) p)

lemma aux_prop (p : M) : p ∈ (aux G p).source :=
  (Classical.choose_spec (isLocalHomeomorph (G := G) (M := M) p)).1

lemma aux_eq (p : M) : aux G p = (Quotient.mk _ : M → (OrbitSpace M G)) :=
  (Classical.choose_spec (isLocalHomeomorph (G := G) (M := M) p)).2.symm

lemma mem_aux_target (p : M) : ⟦p⟧ ∈ (aux G p).target := by
  rw [← OpenPartialHomeomorph.image_source_eq_target, Set.mem_image]
  use p
  refine ⟨aux_prop p, ?_⟩
  sorry -- helper lemma

variable (G) in
def localInverseAt (p : M) : OpenPartialHomeomorph (OrbitSpace M G) M := (aux G p).symm

lemma foo (p : M) : (Quotient.mk _ p) ∈ (localInverseAt G p).source := by

is a Cp-map.

I think this corresponds to my current Lean goal:

⊢ (φx.symm ≫ₕ ρ.toOpenPartialHomeomorph ≫ₕ φy).restr (s ∩ f.source) ∈ (contDiffPregroupoid (↑n) I).groupoid

where the source of f is the source of e^{-1} >> e' (arbitrary chart ats) and s is what in the notes is defined as

ϕi‾(Ui‾′∩Uj‾′)\overline{\phi_i}(\overline{U_i}' \cap \overline{U_j}')ϕi​​(Ui​​′∩Uj​​′)

Great! The definition of C^n actions is actually independent of the other work --- you'll need to add a new definition to mathlib.

Some hints to get you started --- let me know if you get stuck. (I can say more, but don't want to spoil the enjoyment of learning yourself.)

  • you probably want to create a new file (somewhere in Geometry/Manifold); one file for both definitions should suffice for now
  • look at docs#ContinuousSMul for inspiration on "this action is C^n" (basically, you can try and create C^n analogues for all theorems in this file; you can skip stuff like IsScalarTower or OrderDual for now)
  • if you like, you can also look at docs#ContinuousConstSMul for deriving a point-wise version of that

Thinking about this more, I'm hesitant to add a point-wise version: I suspect that all settings we care about will in fact satisfy the stronger hypothesis. In other words, you don't have to do as much work :-)

Hello everyone!

My name is Javier, I have been attending MadLean for a few weeks, and talked with @Pepa Montero Jimena about this project. I believe that the general way to define quotients for differentiable manifolds is to define submersions and apply what is known as Godement's criterion: The quotient will be a manifold if the projection is a submersion. This includes not only the action by a group on a manifold but also more general quotients that may reduce the dimension of the original manifold.

I've seen that @Michael Rothgang and @Samantha Naranjo have an open PR defining submersions for the infinite dimensional case so maybe this should wait until they are finished. I am not sure if there is any plan to make quotient manifolds that general, but I just wanted to get your opinion on this, introduce myself and offer any help you need regarding this project, which I think is very interesting.

Hi Javier! It's great to hear that you're interested in this; thanks for reaching out.

I didn't know about Godement's criterion (though it's actually in Bourbaki, book 10 (differential and analytic manifolds; Section 5.9.5). I haven't checked the statement in detail yet (travelling, so no university wifi), so I don't know how general it is: does it cover manifolds not over the reals or complex numbers? Manifolds with boundary? Infinite-dimensional manifolds?

In any case, this seems like a nice addition to mathlib. (I don't think it should block the current project yet; that statement is a useful special case. If a more general result is proven, the proof can be changed later!) Feel free to work on it. I'll do my best to help. (I should be careful not to promise too much; I've been surprisingly busy recently --- but I certainly want to help.)

Note, though, that Samantha is also working on developing further theory of submersions. As that's part of her master's thesis, it would be nice to not duplicate work. (Take a statement of hers with sorry and moving is one possible strategy, for instance.) I'm sure we can find a solution there!

lemma continuous (x : M) (h : IsSubmersionAtOfComplement F I J n f x) : ContinuousAt f x := by
  obtain ⟨φ, ψ, hφx, hψfx, hφ, hψ, hφψ, ⟨equiv, hequiv⟩⟩ := h
  suffices h' : ContinuousOn f φ.source from h'.continuousAt (φ.open_source.mem_nhds hφx)
  have c := (continuous_fst.comp equiv.continuous).continuousOn.congr hequiv
  rwa [φ.extend_target_eq_image_source, φ.continuousOn_writtenInExtend_iff (by rfl) hφψ] at c

def regular (R : Setoid M) : Prop :=
  ∃ (H' : Type*) (_ : TopologicalSpace H')
  (E' : Type*) (_ : NormedAddCommGroup E') (_ : NormedSpace 𝕜 E')
  (I' : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E' H') (_ : ChartedSpace H' (Quotient R))
  (_ : IsManifold I' n (Quotient R)), IsSubmersion I I' n (Quotient.mk R)

def graph (R : Setoid M) : Set (M × M) := { (x, y) : M × M | R x y }

instance godement (R : Setoid M) : regular R ↔ IsImmersedSubmanifold (graph R) (M × M) := sorry

I'm looking also into the condition of closedness of the graph for T2Space preservation. I think this doesn't need any manifold machinery and can be proved now (maybe someone has already done this?):

instance instT2SpaceQuotient (R : Setoid M) [T2Space M] (h : IsClosed (graph R)) : T2Space (Quotient R) := sorry

smooth action (G : Group) (...) : Prop := ∀ g : G, ContMDiff I I n (fun x ↦ g • x)

FWIW, in case you haven't figured out so already, here is how you could work with the action of a discrete group. In particular, stating "this is a C^n action" is possible already, and (while some learning curve) not too painful.

import Mathlib

open ContDiff Manifold

-- Suppose `Γ` acts on a `C^n` manifold `M`.
variable {𝕜 : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H]
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) (n : ℕ∞ω)
    (Γ : Type*) (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [SMul Γ M]

-- If `Γ` has the discrete topology, we can say "this action is `C^n`" like so.
example [TopologicalSpace Γ] [DiscreteTopology Γ] :
  letI a := ChartedSpace.of_discreteTopology (H := Unit) (M := Γ)
  ContMDiffSMul 𝓘(𝕜, Unit) I n Γ M := sorry

example [SMul ℤ M] :
  letI a := ChartedSpace.of_discreteTopology (H := Unit) (M := ℤ)
  ContMDiffSMul 𝓘(𝕜, Unit) I n ℤ M := sorry

example [SMul (ZMod 2) M] :
  letI a := ChartedSpace.of_discreteTopology (H := Unit) (M := ZMod 2)
  ContMDiffSMul 𝓘(𝕜, Unit) I n (ZMod 2) M := sorry

Michael Rothgang said:

letI a := ChartedSpace.of_discreteTopology

Is it possible to synthesize these instances automatically to avoid having to write this every time?

Quoting the doc-string of docs#ChartedSpace.of_discreteTopology, this could be bad for performance:

We keep this as a definition (not an instance) to avoid instance search trying to search for docs#DiscreteTopology or docs#Unique instances.

You should be able to do attribute [local instance] ChartedSpace.of_discreteTopology to get the same effect in the current file. Indeed, the following works:

import Mathlib

open ContDiff Manifold
-- Suppose `Γ` acts on a `C^n` manifold `M`.
variable {𝕜 : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {H : Type*} [TopologicalSpace H]
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) (n : ℕ∞ω)
    (Γ : Type*) (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M] [SMul Γ M]

attribute [local instance] ChartedSpace.of_discreteTopology
-- If `Γ` has the discrete topology, we can say "this action is `C^n`" like so.
example [TopologicalSpace Γ] [DiscreteTopology Γ] :
  ContMDiffSMul 𝓘(𝕜, Unit) I n Γ M := sorry

example [SMul ℤ M] : ContMDiffSMul 𝓘(𝕜, Unit) I n ℤ M := sorry

example [SMul (ZMod 2) M] : ContMDiffSMul 𝓘(𝕜, Unit) I n (ZMod 2) M := sorry

In general, I would say "yes, but". Review time is super-linear in PR length, so splitting a PR into independent pieces is usually a good idea. For tiny lemmas, it can be helpful to see the big picture. (If they're really obviously good, making them as separate PRs is fine. If it's not so clear where they are used, seeing the overall PR is helpful.)
